**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity).**

- **Clause:** § 7.2 (p0026) — "Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives."
- **Why it fails:** This disclose-and-match gate is a de facto exclusivity / right of first refusal binding us. It covers all Services, runs for the whole term, and has no category limit, no 12-month sunset, and no automatic exit on Vendor's service-level or delivery failures — so it misses the fallback and lands in walk-away territory. It also contradicts § 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges we made no exclusivity or MFC commitment.
- **Redline (validated, ok:true):** delete § 7.2, with a comment offering the fallback (category-limited, 12 months, performance-based termination) if Vendor needs something.
- **Not double-flagged:** § 2.1 take-or-pay minimum volume and § 12.4 non-compete are separate terms for their own rules; § 13.1's non-exclusive licence and § 24.2's competitor-assignment limit benefit us.
